summary: Session 3 of 4 shipped the HTML classification editor as a single-file zero-install tool at tools/classification-editor.html, per the spec's stop-rule in-repo default (the human picked in-repo over a new standalone repo at session start). The editor renders the Session 1 schema's full taxonomy (10-category radio group + 7 masking strategies + preserve-autonumber checkbox per column; 3-state lookup-override radio group + reviewer + notes per table) over a sidebar/content layout, with a sticky reviewer that auto-populates new edits' reviewedBy when blank, file-open via input[type=file] + FileReader, file-save via Blob + URL.createObjectURL + download anchor, Ctrl+S / Ctrl+O shortcuts, an unsaved-changes guard, and a localStorage-backed sticky reviewer. The privacy invariant is honoured: valueFormatPattern is labelled and tooltipped as a structural format (never as a sample value), both notes textareas warn reviewers about pasting raw values, and the editor's pure helpers include a findSuspectNotes heuristic flagging SSN/phone/email patterns. The schema's FK-authority allOf constraint is enforced in the UI (non-FK category radios and non-{preserve,remap-id} masking strategies are disabled for FK columns) and at save time (a confirm dialog blocks silent save of a violating document). Two headless self-tests substitute for the browser-based manual test the spec calls for: tools/classification-editor-self-test.py drives the schema round-trip through editor-like mutations, asserts scanner-emitted fields never drift, and proves FK-authority violations are rejected; tools/classification-editor-js-test.mjs extracts the editor's pure-helper block, evaluates it in a vm context, and asserts CATEGORIES + MASKING_STRATEGIES + SCHEMA_VERSION exactly match the schema's enum + version const. Both tests run green. Two rounds of cross-provider verification by gpt-5-4: R1 ($0.214) surfaced a single Minor finding on the JS test (it checked counts and a hardcoded version literal instead of loading the schema and asserting equality) — fixed in one mechanical change. R2 ($0.133) returned VERIFIED with a bare JSON block (no prose analysis); a R2 prose-first retry was abandoned after the OpenAI 429 rate-limit per the verifier-failure escalation ladder, leaving the bare verdict standing.

reason.specifics: Session 4 is the final session of the set. The FK consistency invariant carries real correctness risk if remap ordering is wrong.
